_what: DATA for check-live-screens.mjs: how a live page is opened and measured, as a person's device opens it. throttle is per width id in views.json: the CPU slowdown (rate, 4 means a phone's processor about four times slower than this one) and the network (latency_ms per request, download_kbps and upload_kbps in kilobits per second; the default is Chrome's Fast 3G throughput at 4G-like latency, 150 ms, not the 562 ms of Chrome's Fast 3G preset). A width with no throttle entry is opened at full speed (desktop). usable_idle_ms is how long the main thread must have run no task longer than 50 ms before a page is usable (the main thread idle for 500 ms, with the ready selector visible). settle_ms is how long a usable page must stay on one document before it counts as settled: a page that sends its whole document through a sign-in hop is measured on the document the person ends on, every time from the moment it was asked for, and the answer's documents lists the addresses it went through. usable_within_ms and navigation_within_ms are the longest a page is waited on before its numbers are answered as they stand (usable_ms null when it never got there). tap_within_ms is the longest a tap may take to show what its expect names before it is answered as not worked. signed_in_gap_ms is the least time between the starts of two signed-in loads in one run: each signed-in load makes 2 sign-in calls (GET /api/auth/oauth2/authorize and POST /api/auth/oauth2/token, counted on a live /home load at 9:53 PM CST Nov 21 2026), which the gateway limits to 20 per 60 s per address, shared by every browser and run on the computer, so 8 s keeps a run to 15 calls a minute and leaves 5 for everything else; closer loads are refused (429) and measured as a broken screen. sign_in_paths are the paths a site sends a signed-out person to: a signed-in view whose page ends on one is answered signed_out true, because it measured the sign-in page and not the screen asked for. inline_png_bytes is the largest picture returned inside the answer as base64 when it cannot be kept in the person's Files (the Files right is missing or refused); a larger one is answered as its 1f: identity only.
